correctness.rationale: JR violation is equivalent to a candidate having at least q=ceil(n/k) supporters unrepresented by W. Laminarity makes distinct supporter sets of cardinality q pairwise disjoint, so r≤floor(n/q)≤k. Any all-quota committee omitting a quota class leaves all q voters of that block unrepresented; thus every such class is mandatory and every DR committee covers exactly U, the union of quota blocks. Selecting one from each is feasible exactly when M≥k (since r≤k), with remaining candidates quota-sized. JR then reduces to |S_c\U|<q for every candidate. Counting labeled nonempty selections by class yields [z^k] product_i((1+z)^w_i−1). Empty classes, duplicate supports, k≥n (q=1), and nonlaminar boundary accounted for; an independent k=5 pair-block enumeration found 32 DR committees among 252 total, matching 2^k/C(2k,k).

value.rationale: An exact feasibility criterion, complete generating-function count, and invariant represented-voter set for a natural hierarchical approval domain are useful structural results within hard committee-selection problems. The pair-block example also quantifies an exponentially small success fraction under uniform lotteries. This is more than a routine renaming of JR; laminarity enforces a strong rigidity theorem and polynomial counting.
